current_example.title: Example: Expressing a Repeating Decimal as the Sum of a Number and a Geometric Series

q-351711.name: Question 1
q-351711.worked_solution:
The given repeating decimal can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}6.\overset{―}{6} & =6.666… \\  & =6+0.6+0.06+0.006+… \\  & ={{6+\frac{6}{10}+\frac{6}{100}+\frac{6}{1\,000}+⋯.}_{⏟}}_{\text{geometric series}}\end{aligned}
$$

We see that we have a geometric series where the first term is ${a}_{1}=6$ and the common ratio is $\frac{1}{10}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}6.\overset{―}{6} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }6{(\frac{1}{10})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }60(\frac{1}{10}){(\frac{1}{10})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }60{(\frac{1}{10})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-5403.name: Question 2
q-5403.worked_solution:
The given repeating decimal can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}0.0\overset{―}{28} & =0.028\,282\,8...… \\  & =0.028+0.000\,28+0.000\,002\,8+… \\  & ={{\frac{28}{1\,000}+\frac{28}{100\,000}+\frac{28}{10\,000\,000}+⋯.}_{⏟}}_{\text{geometric series}}\end{aligned}
$$

We see that we have a geometric series where the first term ${a}_{1}=\frac{28}{1\,000}$ and the common ratio is $r=\frac{1}{100}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}0.0\overset{―}{28} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{28}{1\,000}{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{28}{10}(\frac{1}{100}){(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2.8{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-14114.worked_solution:
The given repeating decimal can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}0.\overset{―}{75} & =0.757\,575… \\  & =0.75+0.007\,5+0.000\,075+… \\  & ={{\frac{75}{100}+\frac{75}{10\,000}+\frac{75}{1\,000\,000}+⋯.}_{⏟}}_{\text{geometric series}}\end{aligned}
$$

We see that we have a geometric series where the first term ${a}_{1}=\frac{75}{100}$ and the common ratio is $r=\frac{1}{100}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}0.\overset{―}{75} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{75}{100}{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }75(\frac{1}{100}){(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }75{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

The given repeating decimal can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}0.\overset{―}{9} & =0.999… \\  & =0.9+0.09+0.009+… \\  & =\frac{9}{10}+\frac{9}{100}+\frac{9}{1\,000}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that we have a geometric series with first term ${a}_{1}=\frac{9}{10}$ and common ratio $r=\frac{1}{10}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}0.\overset{―}{9} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{9}{10}{(\frac{1}{10})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }9(\frac{1}{10}){(\frac{1}{10})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }9{(\frac{1}{10})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
